transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I feel like I just can’t keep my projects organized anymore, no matter how many lists and calendars I use. It's become really overwhelming at work, and I'm just struggling to keep up.
Do you also find it hard to focus on tasks or do you get distracted easily, even when you are trying to pay attention?

Yes, I really struggle with staying focused and get distracted so easily. When I sit down to work on a client deck, I'm only focused for about ten minutes before my mind starts drifting to an email notification or just staring at the wall. I'll suddenly realize I've re-read the same slide notes three times without absorbing any of it.
Did these attention and organization problems start when you were a child or teenager, and do they happen in more than one setting, like at work, at home, or in school?

Yes, they definitely started when I was a kid; my elementary school report cards always mentioned me daydreaming or struggling to stay in my seat, and my mom got so frustrated when I'd leave chores half-finished. Today, it affects me everywhere—I'm currently on a performance improvement plan at work for falling behind on projects, and at home, I'm constantly tearing my apartment apart looking for my work badge or AirPods.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation: longstanding inattention, distractibility, poor sustained attention, disorganization, and forgetfulness beginning in childhood and occurring across multiple settings, with clear occupational and home impairment.
